# Specimen generator output contract

<!-- cspell:words fvar kerx vkrn subtables maxp -->

The specimen generator publishes a self-contained package of native-resolution PNG specimens and display metadata,
independent of the generator's implementation language. This document covers only that published interface.

## Generation selection

[specimens.json](specimens.json) supplies family sources, sizes, renderer variants, and output profiles; the
[configuration guide](README.md#specimen-configuration) defines inheritance and overrides. The resolved configuration
yields explicit family/size/variant/profile cases, one published package per selected renderer variant, verified against
those cases.

When configured, `preview_policy` must match the resolved family/size coverage. Missing or invalid policy or coverage
drift fails before rendering or publication and preserves existing pointers.

`published.json` (schema `specimen-publication-v1`) maps logical variants to packages. Iteration versions are unique
numeric `revision.iteration` pairs compared numerically. Renderer roles select the latest candidate newer than the
baseline against that baseline, or baseline against reference when no newer candidate exists. Without renderer roles,
selection uses the latest iteration against the latest iteration of an earlier revision, or reference when none exists.
The active pointer selects the current input of that comparison, or reference when no iteration exists. The selected
variant and comparison baseline must each have render cases.

## Output location and selection

Paths are relative to the repository root:

```text
out/specimens/
  active.json
  published.json
  <variant-id>/
    manifest.json
    assets/
      <image-sha256>.png
```

The generator owns `out/specimens/`. Each package is immutable: changes to source rendering, sample text, composition,
dimensions, or assets create a new package ID; content-addressed images may be reused when their bytes match.

`active.json` uses schema `web-active-v1` with `variant_id` and `manifest` exactly `<variant_id>/manifest.json`. Variant
IDs are single path segments of ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores.

## Package manifest

`manifest.json` contains these required fields:

| Field                        | Required meaning                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schema_version`             | `web-specimens-v1`                                                                                                    |
| `variant.id`                 | Immutable package identity matching the active pointer                                                                |
| `variant.kind`               | `reference` or `iteration`                                                                                            |
| `variant.version`            | Nonempty human-facing version for an iteration; null for a reference                                                  |
| `variant.generation_sha256`  | SHA-256 identity of the underlying canonical render artifact                                                          |
| `variant.composition_sha256` | SHA-256 identity of the sample/layout composition artifact                                                            |
| `profiles`                   | Definitions of the included configured profiles: `mono_1bit` with output bits 1 and/or `gray_3bit` with output bits 3 |
| `families`                   | Ordered family records with a stable `id`, display `name`, original-font `source_sha256`, and `sizes`                 |

Exports include each family's descriptive `metadata`; consumers also accept packages without it. It has these fields:
`names` (nullable `family`, `style`, `full`, `postscript`, `version`, `copyright`, `manufacturer`, `designer`,
`description`, `vendor_url`, `designer_url`, `license`, `license_url`); `axes` (source-ordered `tag`, nullable `name`,
`min`, `default`, `max`, `hidden`); `glyph_count` (nullable total from `maxp.numGlyphs`, including unencoded glyphs;
absent in older packages); `font_hints` (nullable source hint presence, absent in older packages; actual TrueType glyph
instructions or PostScript stem/alignment hints, without a quality or axis-coverage claim); `kerning` (`horizontal`,
`vertical`, and `sources` drawn from `GPOS kern`, `GPOS vkrn`, `kern`, `kerx`); `style` (nullable `slope` of
`upright`/`italic`/`oblique`, raw `weight_class` and `width_class`, `italic_angle` in degrees); `classification`
(nullable raw IBM `family_class`, ten-byte `panose`, `monospaced`); `coverage` (nullable `character_count` and sorted,
disjoint, inclusive scalar `ranges`); and `declared_unicode_ranges` (nullable four OS/2 range words). Definitions follow
the OpenType [name](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/name),
[fvar](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/fvar),
[maxp](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/maxp),
[OS/2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/os2), and
[kern](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/kern) specifications.

Each family has a nonempty `sizes` array; array order is the intended presentation order. Each size group contains
`size_px`, the resolved `axes` coordinates, a `thumbnail` (`width_px`, `height_px`, shared by every image in the group),
and explicitly ordered `items`, each appearing once per family and size. Each item has a package-wide unique `id`,
`profile`, `label`, exact sample `text`, and `outcome`: `rendered` includes `image.path` of the form
`assets/<image.sha256>.png` with `image.sha256`; `failed` or `unsupported` includes a nonempty `reason`.

## Specimen images

Each PNG is composed at native resolution, its dimensions equal the group's declared thumbnail dimensions. Encoding is
lossless PNG on a white background: black/white pixels for 1-bit specimens, the declared eight display levels for 3-bit.
Failures and unsupported samples appear only through item outcomes and reasons, never as substitute images.

## Glyph comparison export

Comparison inputs and labels derive from [generation selection](#generation-selection) and package versions. A
reference-only publication exports an empty comparison index; invalid or ambiguous versions fail publication.

The exporter publishes:

```text
out/specimens/comparisons/
  index.json
  <id>-<manifest-sha256>/
    manifest.json
    assets/<image-sha256>.png
```

`index.json` uses schema `web-comparisons-v1` with entries containing `id` and `manifest`. Each manifest uses
`web-glyph-comparison-v1`, identifies its two input packages and labels, and contains profiles and families with
ascending size groups, resolved axes, and a shared canvas (`width_px`, `height_px`, `origin_x`, `baseline_y`,
`padding_px`) under one baseline and pen origin.

Each glyph record declares `codepoint`, `character`, and selected `profiles`. Each profile includes `id`, rounded native
`advance_px`, and `previous`, `current`, and `difference` image references (`path`, `sha256`, `reason` null), exported
only when aligned native pixels differ. Difference images use blue `#0060ff` for increased ink and red `#e02020` for
decreased ink; unchanged pixels retain their shade.

Each manifest carries a `statistics` array with one record per profile: `profile`, `same_symbols`, `changed_symbols`,
`average_changed_pixels`, and `median_changed_pixels`. Each drawable character counts once per family/size/profile,
including identical glyphs omitted from image records; a changed pixel is an aligned native pixel whose quantized value
differs, and averages/medians over changed symbols are zero when none changed. Missing glyphs, cases, inputs, or render
reports fail publication with identifying details and leave the existing comparison index unchanged.

## Publication checks

Publishing guarantees: schema versions, pointer/package identity, safe variant IDs, and SHA-256 values agree; family
identities, resolved axes, size groups, and item IDs are unique and complete against the resolved configuration; profile
references and outcome-specific fields are valid; assets exist with matching hashes, native dimensions, and pixel
levels; and every relative path resolves within its package, including through symlinks. A complete, validated package
is published before any pointer or index update; each update is atomic.
# Generator API

<!-- cspell:words fpgm SCANCTRL SCANTYPE Playdate interglyph pdfontconv unrepresentable -->

This interface covers native generation, renderer selection and layout consumed by the WASM and specimen adapters.
[Setup, commands and settings defaults](README.md) are separate from the [published specimen contract](CONTRACT.md).
Renderer identities and model decisions belong to the [revision index](../../docs/revisions/001/README.md#iterations).

## Supported input and output

Input is one sfnt TTF/OTF with glyf, CFF or CFF2 outlines, fixed or variable. Collections, WOFF/WOFF2, bitmap-only and
color fonts require a separate adapter or conversion. Axis tags and values are checked against the font; omitted axes
use its defaults. Missing glyphs either fail or are listed as skipped, according to settings.

The repertoire supports Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and common symbols. Combining marks, control/format characters and other
scripts fail with unsupported-shaping errors. HarfRust resolves each isolated scalar at the requested axes. One-to-one
substitutions, including
[required variation alternates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/features_pt#tag-rvrn), select
the glyph used for outlines, geometry, advances and kerning. `codepoint` retains Unicode identity; `glyph_id` records
the glyph drawn and can differ from the nominal character map.

Optional ligatures/contextual alternates are disabled. Each scalar must produce exactly one non-missing glyph without
positioning. Offsets, vertical advances and standalone horizontal advance adjustments fail; the latter are checked
against the shaper's own metric before positioning or pixel rounding, preserving fractional linear source metrics. Pairs
must preserve the isolated glyph IDs, order and count; only a left-advance adjustment is representable.
Context-dependent substitutions, offsets and right-advance changes fail. Complete text-run shaping requires a separate
adapter.

`generate(font_bytes, &Config)` returns sorted glyphs, skipped codepoints, sorted nonzero kerning pairs and line
metrics. Pixels are row-major **unpacked** levels from zero (no ink) to `2^output_bits - 1` (full ink). `left` and `top`
locate the bitmap relative to a baseline in y-down coordinates; empty glyphs retain advances. Advances, pair
adjustments, ascent, descent and line gap use signed 26.6 pixels (divide by 64). Ascent/descent retain font signs,
conventionally positive ascent and negative descent; line spacing is ascent minus descent plus line gap. Add pair
adjustments to the left advance.

Outlines are hinted as requested; `generate` uses variation-aware linear advances with explicit output rounding.
Consumers place origins on the pixel grid; fractional-origin rasterization and LVGL packing are outside this interface.

With the `candidate` feature, `candidate::generate_bitmap_font(font_bytes, &Config, strategy)` exports 1-bit or 3-bit
strikes with candidate bitmaps/offsets, whole-pixel advances and sparse whole-pixel pair adjustments. Other depths fail.
The `*_26_6` fields still encode pixels in multiples of 64. Consumers accumulate these metrics according to the
[spacing contract](#live-spacing-api); the optional strategy affects Mono and is ignored for Gray strikes.
`candidate::generate_bitmap_font_with_tracking(font_bytes, &Config, strategy, letter_spacing_px)` bakes uniform tracking
into those advances; bitmaps, offsets and pair adjustments remain unchanged.

## Playdate font export

`playdate::export(font_bytes, &ExportRequest)` returns a standalone UTF-8 `.fnt` with an embedded PNG image table, glyph
widths and sparse signed pair adjustments, following the
[Playdate source-font format](https://sdk.play.date/Inside%20Playdate.html#_fonts). `ExportRequest` contains `config:
Config`, `pipeline: RenderPipeline` and `letter_spacing_px` (default zero). The candidate feature and 1-bit output are
required. The selected stages, axes, repertoire, scan settings, kerning and uniform tracking produce the same finalized
bitmap metrics as explicit-pipeline preview. Tracking is already included in advances; the consumer must not add it
again. `playdate::encode(&GeneratedFont)` serializes an existing finalized strike without refitting or rounding its
metrics.

The supported export subset has 1–1024 distinct characters within U+0020–U+3FFFF, excluding controls and unsupported
shaping. Missing glyphs fail even with `missing_glyphs: "skip"`. Dimensions and advances are limited to 255 pixels;
advances must be nonnegative integers and pair adjustments must be integers within -128–127 pixels. Cells share the
preview baseline and line height. Every cell shifts right by a common inset covering the leftmost actual ink across the
export, following [pdfontconv](https://github.com/ttencate/pdfontconv/blob/main/main.js); the inset folds into shared
tracking so each pen advance and interglyph step is unchanged. Playdate-reported text bounds include the terminal cell
padding after the final glyph, so measured widths exceed the source advance sums by that padding. Transparent scanner
padding imposes no ink bounds; only actual ink constrains the inset. Ink outside the line cell vertically fails with the
codepoint rather than being clipped or shifted. The image table is limited to 16,777,216 pixels.

Widths plus shared tracking reproduce finalized advances; shared tracking can be negative to retain the common left
inset and right overhangs. Pair adjustments are unchanged. An informational `--origin_x` header records the inset and is
ignored by Playdate; it is omitted when zero so those outputs stay byte-identical. Glyph entries precede pair entries
and use explicit Unicode names. Glyphs and pairs are ordered by codepoint. For equal inputs and implementation, native
and WASM exports are byte-identical. Invalid or unrepresentable data returns an error without a partial font.

## Renderer routing

`generate` uses the separate `vendor/skrifa-baseline` snapshot for automatic Mono fitting. Independent reference capture
uses registry Skrifa. The optional `candidate` feature exposes registry-backed fitting; disabling it leaves production
on the baseline. Versions are metadata, not per-iteration Cargo features. `iteration` remains a compatibility alias for
`candidate`, not a production renderer selector.

For production `auto_fallback`, embedded interpretation remains embedded and selected automatic Mono uses the legacy
custom policy. Explicit `interpreter` and `none` preserve those paths. Gray production uses symmetric Normal rendering
with linear metric preservation. The [baseline patch policy](vendor/skrifa-baseline/PATCH.md) owns its maintenance
rules.

### Working candidate fitting

`surface::PreparedFont::new(Vec<u8>)` owns immutable font bytes. Its `render_text_with_fitting_strategy` and
`render_text_with_pipeline_and_spacing` methods accept the same request, selection and tracking arguments as the
corresponding raw-byte functions, with identical validation and output. `as_bytes()` provides read-only access; there is
no byte-replacement operation. Reuse must preserve validation and output independently of preceding requests, eviction
and the lifetime of other prepared fonts. Raw-byte entry points retain identical output without shared cache state.

Current native preview clients use `surface::render_text_with_pipeline(font_bytes, &TextRenderRequest, RenderPipeline)`.
`RenderPipeline` separates `fitting` (`font_hints_auto`, `font_hints_first`, `source_relative` or `upstream_mono`) from
`rasterization` (`free_type_mono`, `free_type_mono_terminals` or `coverage`). It requires the `candidate` feature.
Optional `diagonal_fitting` defaults to `false`; `true` requires 1-bit FreeType scan conversion with `font_hints_auto`
or `upstream_mono`. Its fixed donor reference is independent of the requested text. Unsupported geometry retains the
preceding fitted outline. The [fitting design](../../docs/hobby-fitting.md#approved-fitting-sequence-adoption) owns the
model and gates. Modified captures identify `diagonal-shape-04` and retain the original upstream outline, donor
reference and unrounded feature source for independent replay; the preference does not change metrics or layout. Fitting
owns engine selection and returned advances; rasterization consumes the fitted outline without changing geometry or
metrics. Both scanners use the same bitmap layout below, with uniform extra tracking defaulting to zero. In 1-bit
output, coverage is Zeno Alpha quantized using `mono_threshold`; FreeType uses the scan controls below. Coverage rejects
non-default `mono_raster` settings. In 2-, 3- or 4-bit output, only automatic fitting (`upstream_mono`) with `coverage`
is valid; this uses Normal fitting. Invalid combinations fail even for blank text. Historical role APIs remain available
with their original fitting, rasterization and layout policies.

Candidate Mono uses Skrifa 0.48.0 `Target::Mono` on runtime font bytes, including user-provided fonts:

| Strategy                     | Extension            | Engine                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `font_hints_first` (default) | `font-hints-01`      | Automatic Mono for verified program-free fonts, otherwise `Engine::AutoFallback`                                                          |
| `upstream_mono`              | `mono-width-01`      | `Engine::Auto(None)`: automatic fitting, ignoring embedded instructions                                                                   |
| `source_relative`            | `source-width-01`    | Font hints first, followed by conservative source-relative straight-stroke fitting on automatic outlines                                  |
| `font_hints_auto`            | `font-hints-auto-01` | Native fitting on controlled axes, automatic fitting on the remaining axes; retains source-relative correction on wholly automatic glyphs |

`font_hints_auto` requires 1-bit output and a FreeType scan stage. TrueType axis ownership records executed point
constraints and coordinate measurements, including zero-distance …58 tokens truncated…cs follow the X-axis fitting owner; executed font
scan controls remain authoritative when requested. Historical strategies keep their existing behavior. The
[iteration note](../../docs/revisions/001/03-spacing-kerning.md#selective-native-hints-and-automatic-fitting) owns the
model's assumptions and assessment limits.

[Upstream engine selection](https://docs.rs/skrifa/0.48.0/skrifa/outline/enum.Engine.html) considers TrueType glyph
instructions and nonempty `fpgm`/`prep`; CFF/CFF2 uses its interpreter. This selects an engine without assessing hint
quality. On TrueType fonts verified to carry no glyph instruction streams, no `fpgm`, and an absent or scan-control-only
`prep`, `font_hints_first` uses upstream automatic Mono fitting instead of upstream selection; every other font keeps
upstream selection. The request stays `auto_fallback` while each record's `selected_engine` reports the actual engine.
No Mono strength or diagonal-balance controls are exposed. The original two policies use whole upstream-fitted outlines.
The default rasterization is the pinned FreeType 2.15.0 monochrome scanner: nonzero-winding center fill with
two-direction sweeps and upstream overshoot handling. The scanner receives nearest-rounded 26.6 points (ties towards
positive infinity) at the existing integer origin. Candidate Mono ignores `mono_threshold`; raw Zeno Alpha coverage is
diagnostic and does not determine its delivered pixels on the FreeType path. FreeType captures declare `raster_policy:
"free_type_mono"`, `mono_rasterizer` with the scanner version and compiled vendored-source SHA-256, and per-record
effective `mono_raster` settings. FreeType does no font loading, hinting or layout here.

`free_type_mono_terminals` retains the same fitting and layout, then suppresses smart-dropout rescues only at straight
caps certified against both the source and fitted outlines. Ambiguous features keep the original scan; executed font
instructions remain authoritative. It requires 1-bit output. Captures use `raster_policy: "free_type_mono_terminals"`
and include `source_commands` for independent identity checks and raster reproduction. The
[iteration assessment](../../docs/revisions/001/03-spacing-kerning.md#terminal-tips-and-junction-continuity) owns the
model and assessment scope.

`source_relative` requires 1-bit FreeType scan conversion. It preserves returned advances and engine selection;
unsupported or uncertain features retain the upstream outline. Modified records include `source_commands` and
`width_fitting: { size_px, upstream_commands }` so evaluation can verify independent source/input identity and reproduce
the correction. Its policy identifier remains selected when no feature qualifies; `width_fitting` is absent on each
unchanged record. The [source-width model](../../docs/hobby-fitting.md#valid-straight-medial-intervals) owns geometric
eligibility and limits.

Records changed by `diagonal_fitting` additionally carry `diagonal_fitting: { model, size_px, upstream_commands,
native_axes, reference, reason, raw_source? }`. `reference` contains the captured upright anchors; `raw_source` retains
the unrounded feature input when available. Earlier width/selective captures describe `upstream_commands`; the record's
final commands and scan policy reproduce its bitmap.

### Monochrome scan-converter settings

`Config.mono_raster` defaults to `{"dropout":"smart","include_stubs":false,"font_instructions":false}`. `dropout`
accepts `smart`, `simple`, or `off`; `include_stubs` preserves short strokes and has no effect when dropout is `off`.
Absent fields default; unknown modes or fields fail. Non-default settings require candidate Mono, including for blank
requests; legacy generation, independent reference, probes and other output depths reject them.

Opt-in `font_instructions` follows executed TrueType `SCANCTRL` and `SCANTYPE`, including component contour markers,
when the selected engine is the embedded TrueType interpreter. Automatic fitting, CFF/CFF2, variable composite outlines
and disabled hinting retain the manual settings as fallback. Engine selection is unchanged. This path draws with a
pinned metadata-only Skrifa snapshot; fitting algorithms are unchanged, registry Skrifa remains independent for
manual/reference/Gray paths, and captures identify the patch in `implementation` with `fork: true` when it is used.
Per-record `font_scan` contains its source SHA-256, final `enabled` and full 16-bit `scan_type`, and contour-ordered
`contour_modes` (`null` inherits the preceding mode; integers 0–7 mark a new mode). Global invalid scan types disable
dropout; only contour markers truncate to three bits, matching FreeType. Evaluation reconstructs pixels from recorded
settings and scan state, rejecting incompatible state, invalid markers or mismatched source identity. This does not
assert full FreeType driver equivalence.

Candidate Mono accepts at most 65,535 scan-converter points per glyph; invalid geometry or allocation-limit violations
fail explicitly without a coverage fallback. `vertical_only` and `vertical-01` are rejected.

Historical native text clients call `surface::render_text_with_fitting_strategy` with role, tracking and an optional
`StemFittingStrategy`; omission selects `FontHintsFirst`. Selection normalizes effective hinting to `auto_fallback` for
font hints first or `auto` for forced auto. Candidate automatic inputs `auto`/`auto_fallback` are accepted; `none` and
`interpreter` fail. Explicit strategies require the candidate feature, candidate role and 1-bit output, even for blank
text. Incompatible requests fail. Capture `hinting_requested` records the effective policy; each record's
`selected_engine` reports `interpreter` or `auto`. Gray retains upstream Normal automatic fitting without a Mono
strategy selector. The independent reference requires an explicit engine.

## Reference and specimen capture

`reference::reference(font_bytes, &ReferenceRequest)` captures independently of production `generate` and job defaults.
The `font_reference JOB.json OUTPUT.json` adapter accepts `font`, `provenance`, `settings`, `profile` (`mono_1bit` or
`gray_3bit`) and optional `extensions` (default `none`). Select hinting explicitly as `auto`, `interpreter` or `none`,
with matching output bits 1 or 3. `auto_fallback`, unknown fields, mismatched targets and unsupported extensions fail.

Configured reference specimens use Skrifa 0.48.0 `Engine::Auto(None)`, extensions `none` and Zeno 0.3.3 Alpha coverage:
Mono uses `Target::Mono`, threshold 128; Gray uses `SmoothMode::Normal.into()` (symmetric rendering true, preserve
linear metrics false), gamma 1 and `round(7 * coverage / 255)`. Engine/target selection follows the pinned
[Fontations harness](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontations/blob/f886c9069b08eaddcb1caced3a44b0d8291a159a/fauntlet/src/font/mod.rs)
and
[Skrifa target settings](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontations/blob/f886c9069b08eaddcb1caced3a44b0d8291a159a/skrifa/src/outline/hint.rs).
[Nearest-level quantization](../../docs/references/papers/2006-gallager-quantization/) (§3.2.1, p. 65) converts
coverage; this adapted reference differs from default `AutoFallback` and
[TrueType monochrome scan conversion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/ttch01#the-scan-converter).
Panel tone mapping is separate.

Reports retain controls, dependency identities, fitted-command f32 bits, raw coverage, quantized pixels and placement.
Reference, baseline, candidate and diagnostic capture resolve the same selected glyph IDs at the requested axes, with
renderer-specific fitting and advance policies. See the [diagnostics guide](../../docs/references/font-diagnostics.md).

Specimens use selected-renderer layout with HarfRust run adjustments, kerning enabled and optional ligature/contextual
features disabled. Candidate uses bitmap placement; reference/baseline use source-linear layout. Published images follow
the [specimen output contract](CONTRACT.md#specimen-images).

## Live spacing API

Explicit pipelines share bitmap layout with optional uniform tracking; there is no selectable spacing model.
`surface::render_text_with_pipeline` defaults to zero; `surface::render_text_with_pipeline_and_spacing` accepts the
tracking offset. Historical role APIs retain their layout policies. Baseline `generate()` and independent reference use
fractional source advances and kerning, accumulated in 26.6 and rounded only when drawing. Their source-layout captures
are diagnostic controls.

Candidate Mono and Gray use the same bitmap policy in exported strikes, native specimens and preview:

- Each advance is finalized in whole pixels from the fitter's returned advance, or the rounded source advance when
  unavailable. Source-tabular digits (equal advances for all ten digits at the exact axes) retain the common quantized
  source advance. Fixed-pitch fonts and tabular digits carry no fitted bearing deltas.
- Source kerning and available fitted bearing corrections resolve once into sparse whole-pixel pair adjustments.
  Captures without bearing deltas contribute no correction. Disabling kerning removes the source contribution; fitting
  correction may still apply. `ascii_kerning_pairs` describes source data independently.
- Values round to nearest whole pixels, ties away from zero, preserving signed symmetry. Neutral tracking has no
  blank-column floor; intentional overhang remains. Integer pen accumulation gives each pair the same relative placement
  regardless of preceding text; line widths and wrapping use these metrics.

`layout_spacing::SpacingEngine::place` consumes finalized advances, pair kerning and bearing deltas, returning the glyph
origin and next pen. Native layout, interactive drawing, specimens and wrapping share that operation; exported candidate
metrics are exactly their inputs.

### Tracking policy

Offsets are finite, -16 to +16 px, with zero neutral. Explicit-pipeline tracking rounds to whole pixels with half ties
away from zero, for both Mono and Gray. It adds the same signed offset to every finalized glyph advance, including
spaces and the final glyph advance. Zero and negative resulting advances remain signed; per-glyph clamping, minimum-gap
floors and word-gap refunds do not apply. Bitmaps, offsets and finalized pair adjustments remain unchanged. Rendering,
measurement, wrapping and tracked bitmap export use these same adjusted advances; consumers of a tracked strike must not
apply the tracking again. Additional pair corrections are unnecessary in this signed metric representation.

Historical role APIs retain protected tracking: Mono and candidate Gray use whole pixels, while baseline/reference Gray
retain fractional 26.6 offsets. Nonzero Mono tracking preserves a blank column for normally separated source pairs,
except fixed pitch and tabular digits. Negative tracking preserves neutral ASCII word gaps; positive tracking widens
letters and spaces. These historical constraints can limit tightening. Static publication uses zero tracking. Rationale
belongs to the [tracking decision](../../docs/revisions/001/03-spacing-kerning.md#tracking-and-word-separation).
# Web output contract

Paths below are relative to the repository root.

- `just web` writes a self-contained static app to `out/web/`, independent of `out/specimens` and generator
  configuration. It serves from `out/web/` beneath any hosting URL prefix and exposes no font-upload endpoint: fonts
  stay in the browser-local library.
- The build consumes the candidate-enabled standard SIMD preview renderer at `tools/wasm/pkg-web-preview-simd128/`
  through the [WASM interface](../wasm/README.md) and the canonical font bytes in `fonts/`; both inputs arrive
  unchanged. Missing preview renderer artifacts fail the production build. The default renderer requires WebAssembly
  SIMD support; `FONT_WASM_PREVIEW_DIR` may select a scalar preview package for a separate compatible build.
- Published files include `index.html`, hashed JS/CSS/renderer/font/license assets, `manifest.webmanifest`, and the
  service worker (`sw.js`, scope `./`).
- Routes live in the URL fragment under the one static document, so no server rewrites are needed: `#/` shows the font
  library, `#/font/<content-id>/?v=1…` shows that font's unsaved preview with its versioned settings, and
  `#/font/<content-id>/variant/<variant-id>/` shows one saved variant whose settings live in the browser-local database,
  never in the URL. `#/palettes/` shows the standalone palette lab, independent of the font library with no palette
  state in the URL. Palette presets (including the read-only Monochrome preset) live in the same browser-local database.
  Presets contain 2, 4, 8 or 16 gray levels; saved font settings reference a preset by ID, defaulting to Monochrome when
  absent or unavailable. Unsaved preview snapshots carry this browser-local reference as `palette`; another browser
  without that preset uses Monochrome. Legacy `?font=<content-id>` snapshots and `#family-<content-id>` links migrate to
  the hash route. An unknown font id or route shows the library with a recovery notice.
- Unsaved preview snapshots encode optional diagonal fitting as `diagonals=1`; omission means disabled. Saved variants
  store the same preference in their settings. Rendering and export forward it through the shared pipeline contract.
# Playdate Font Lab staging

Builds `out/playdate-font-lab/FontLab.pdx` from `tools/playdate/Source/` plus generated fonts.

## Setup

Install the Playdate SDK 3.1.2 (provides `bin/pdc` and the Simulator) and point at it:

```sh
export PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH="$HOME/Developer/PlaydateSDK"
```

Needs Node and, for the default export, Rust/Cargo with a C compiler. Generated output under `out/playdate-font-lab/` is
not committed. SDK fonts and installed SDK assets are never copied into the repo.

## Commands

```sh
node tools/playdate/build.mjs --help
node tools/playdate/build.mjs
node tools/playdate/build.mjs --font path/to/custom.fnt --run
```

## Configuration

- `--sdk PATH` overrides `PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH`; with neither set, falls back to `~/Developer/PlaydateSDK`. An explicit
  `--sdk` or a set `PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH` without `bin/pdc` stops the build instead of falling back.
- Without `--font`, exports repo `fonts/Roboto.ttf` and `fonts/SourceSans3.ttf` at 16/24 px via `cargo run --bin
  font_playdate`, one kerned/plain partner pair each; request JSON lands in `out/playdate-font-lab/requests/`.
- `--font PATH` (repeatable) stages an existing Playdate `.fnt` without invoking Rust; entries carry no `unkerned`
  partner and coverage is derived from the file. Staged copies are named `provided-<n>-<slug>.fnt`; labels keep the
  original filename.
- `--text TEXT` / `--text-file PATH` (repeatable, combine in argument order) stage custom inspection phrases in
  `Source/phrases.lua`, always written and empty when none. A file's whole UTF-8 content is one phrase; tabs become
  spaces. Empty phrases, control characters other than LF, malformed UTF-8, phrases over 4096 scalars, and more than 16
  phrases stop the build.
- Without `--font`, phrase scalars join the printable-ASCII repertoire at the default 16/24 px sizes; missing glyphs
  fail the export. Imported `--font` coverage is unchanged, so phrases render only supported glyphs.
- `--run` opens the compiled `.pdx` in the SDK Simulator.
# Development revisions

Revisions group iterations; each iteration groups related topics for review: corrections, improvements, capabilities or
investigations.

## Folder structure

- `README.md`: this guide.
- `NNN/README.md`: revision starting point, renderer identities and iteration index with brief outcomes or status.
- `NNN/NN-topic.md`: iteration design and decision note; for example, `001/02-light-continuity.md` is iteration 001.02.

## Iteration documents

Write a design and decision note, grouping topics by a shared goal, model or invariant rather than by glyph or work
step:

- **Title and introduction:** motivation and adopted approach.
- **Foundation and invariant:** shared sources and preserved relationships. Follow the
  [evaluation rules](../evaluation.md); label project hypotheses. Put distinct foundations beside their topics.
- **Topics:** one subsection per topic, numbered when useful, explaining the logic change and rationale. Retain rejected
  alternatives only when they explain a decision or constraint.
- **Scope and limits:** applicability, accepted review scope, limitations and unresolved work or assigned follow-up.
  Keep essential assessment evidence beside the relevant topic or limitation.

Describe the resulting behavior, not its implementation, testing or publication history. Replace superseded proposals;
omit file maps, handoffs, command/build logs, verification ledgers and artifact metadata. Keep detailed diagnostics
elsewhere. Avoid repeated status, unchanged-state reminders and document-routing prose; unchanged behavior matters only
as an invariant or scope boundary.

## Documentation ownership

The revision index owns lifecycle status, closure dates and renderer identities; iteration notes own model decisions and
scoped assessment. Evaluation principles belong in the [evaluation guide](../evaluation.md); commands, APIs and
interface contracts belong in tool documentation. Preview selections belong in configuration and policy files. Link to
the owner rather than repeat its content. Vendored baseline/candidate documentation remains independent.

## Iteration lifecycle

Feedback may extend an iteration's agreed topics. Close only with explicit user agreement and a disposition for each:
completed, accepted with limits, declined or deferred to a specific follow-up. Passing tests, publishing a preview or
completing one topic does not close the group. Advance numbering after closure, with the next scope agreed from
feedback.

uses Skrifa 0.48.0. The vendored 001.02 implementation is a legacy comparison model; its baseline role name does not

# Domain Correctness

Review domain models, traversal, validation, transformation, serialization,
persistence, generated output, and stable user-facing identifiers. Use supplied
domain invariants and proof requirements. Trace changed data from accepted input
through the actual production path to final output and rejection/cleanup.

Challenge these failure classes when applicable:

- schema, persistence, runtime validation, and interactive admission disagree;
  include exact-limit and one-over-limit proof for collection constraints;
- creation defaults and explicit names violate the validator's uniqueness
  rules. Check occupied generated names and normalized requested collisions
  through each creation entry point, including legacy consumers;
- incomplete variants emit placeholders, discard valid falsy values, or perform
  lookups requiring a completed value;
- read-only traversal mutates persisted/plain data or assumes Immer drafts;
- typed accessors promise shapes they did not validate;
- destructive imports miss alternate references, aliases, overlays, or lexical
  trivia. Require source preservation or rejection when unsupported syntax
  leaves reference integrity or conditions uncertain;
- validators leak dependency wording, turn malformed data into ordinary guidance,
  or use presence checks where definedness is required;
- a generic resolver derives identity from feature-specific literals or
  locale-sensitive formatting;
- independently derived representations, indexes, lookups, traversal,
  collision/deduplication, merge, generation, or exemption paths disagree on
  canonical semantic identity;
- a staged change gains authority to update a persisted entity through name
  equality rather than its owned target. Trace target ownership across staging
  origins and nesting, refreshed persisted state, validation exemptions, and
  publication; compose conflicting and authorized paths in observable proof;
- a structured subject, path, or descriptor coordinate is projected into a
  different coordinate space without proving compatible identity and
  cardinality, such as treating an aggregate branch position as an item row.

For new persisted fields or changed cross-layer constraints, inventory owning
entities, mutating entry points, and affected invariants. Check preservation on
replacement and reference remapping or removal on move, copy, and delete.
Require an observable output/failure assertion that kills a plausible mutant,
not only a helper-level test.
# Architecture

Use the supplied architecture and coding standards. Focus on cohesion,
duplicated rules, public/type boundaries, folder topology, readable predicates,
and applicable local limits. File only changes that remove real indirection,
duplicated ownership, or ambiguity while retaining a clear domain boundary.

For every assigned `code-surface-conciseness` row, record each path as
`reduction candidate`, `no meaningful reduction`, or `out of scope` with a
reason. Do not equate fewer lines, arbitrary file splitting, or denser syntax
with a reduction.

For changed transactions/lifecycles with multiple identities, build a terminal
effect closure across success, rollback, partial completion, supersession, and
owner retirement. Trace each invalidated identity through cached, persisted,
notification, callback, and derived resources. Also challenge stale consumers
of retired result contracts, unsafe type recovery at schema boundaries, and
identity helpers that compare too few fields.
# Test Quality

Review changed unit, integration, browser, and helper proof. Look for tests
that can pass with missing behavior, optional assertions, fixed sleeps, leaked
global resources, brittle copy/class selectors, and claims stronger than their
assertions.

Check finding closure at the nearest stable public boundary. For absence,
fallback, or no-op tests, start with conflicting state so skipped work or a
leaked fallback makes the test fail.

For identity-sensitive async proof, compare the harness's callback and resource
lifetimes with their production producers. A stable mock cannot establish
coalescing across renders when the real dependency is recreated. Require an
unchanged-input request across a rerender alongside semantic-change replacement,
checking the operation count and final result. Use the real dependency or a
faithful lifetime model only at the boundary under test; do not remove unrelated
mocks or infer a user-visible path from direct hook calls alone.

For actions that remove the focused control or an overlay's return-focus target,
require a mounted keyboard test with an explicit final-focus assertion after
cleanup. Setting and visibility assertions alone do not prove focus continuity;
include disabled destinations and the surviving fallback.

For dialog focus closure, require the real dialog lifecycle, including deferred
cleanup and StrictMode replay when enabled by the host. An editor mock that
omits close-autofocus cannot prove ownership survives cleanup while still open.
When transitions share reveal, selection, or session state, check whether one
changes the other's guard or identity. If it does, require the reachable combined
scenario through final focus, or demonstrate independence from the consumer's
actual guards. Separate passing tests or a shared helper alone do not establish
independence; unrelated states need no combination matrix.

For gesture ownership changes, switch the owner while the gesture remains
active, then deliver completion and assert the successor's state is preserved.
Clearing the manual flag or ending the gesture before switching proves only
retirement, not completion through the successor's callbacks.

For shared persistence records, seed competing configurations with overlapping
IDs and different values. Assert both the restored active result and unchanged
siblings after mount and update; a single-configuration fixture cannot prove
selection or preservation.
Include omitted optional IDs across remounts, legacy keys with different sort
orders, and throwing custom reads/writes. Fixture guards must not supply the
failure isolation claimed for the production adapter.

For a production-path claim, apply supplied proof requirements:
the first observable checkpoint must precede fixture, mock, click, focus, or
recovery steps that could inject or repair the claimed state. Name a plausible
mutant and the assertion that kills it.

Check schema fixtures against their real types; test callbacks and admission
statuses through their competing fallback paths; use stable semantic selectors;
and prove geometry/scroll movement for responsive overflow. In pointer and drag
browser tests, sample destination geometry after activation or another
rendering transition before using it; do not carry pre-transition coordinates
into the changed layout. Require direct tests for changed pure recursive helpers
and explicit teardown for resources outside renderer ownership. For async
derived UI, prove initial and transition states, not only an eventual result.
# Adversarial Tooling And Boundaries

Use for scripts, git/shell/process wrappers, CLI or environment parsing,
path/glob handling, CI, audit output, and parsers of external command output.
Assign the Scope Inventory key `adversarial-tooling-boundary`.

Challenge argv/option injection, path containment, malformed or future command
output, trim/normalization drift, rename/delete/copy metadata, machine-output
rows with empty fields, delimiter collisions, and filtered values that differ
from values later reported or executed. An empty malformed path must never
become the repository root or current directory.

Include **Edge Assumptions Challenged** in the response: e.g. leading `-`,
embedded delimiters, missing/blank values, whitespace, unknown status codes,
renames, and malformed external rows. Check whether external tuple fields can
collide when combined into a cache or de-duplication key.
# React Rendering

Review TSX components, hooks, virtualized panels, layout state, rendering
lifecycle, performance-sensitive identity, accessibility, and translate-safe
content. Look for stale closures, controlled/uncontrolled drift, desynchronised
derived state, unnecessary hot-path renders, and component ownership ambiguity.

Challenge semantic keys that omit ordering, duplication, or normalisation
meaningful to the consumer. For global DOM state or registrations, trace update,
ownership transfer, deactivation, and unmount so stale cleanup cannot clear a
successor. For reusable components, verify prop surfaces describe actual local
behavior; caller classes merge correctly; and repeated mounted instances have
unique IDs.

For in-flight request identity, inspect both equality directions: equivalent
requests must still join after a rerender, and changed semantic inputs must
replace the running operation. Trace callback producers before treating their
references as request data; distinguish implementation churn from changes to
the captured execution environment. Inspect request equality separately from
owner lifetime and publication authority. This check applies when request
coalescing or replacement changes, not to every hook dependency array.

For overlay eligibility changes, apply the interaction-ownership check in
[Hotkeys And Races](hotkeys-and-races.md) across rendering and keyboard handling.

For dependency adapters, check retained optional props and upstream defaults
with both ordinary and app-specific implementations. For persistence, trace
restoration before startup writes and check owner identity at every writer.
A custom storage guard or final-flush guard does not protect other write paths.
When a storage record holds multiple configurations, check exact configuration
selection and sibling preservation at every writer, including restoration replay
and final flush. Distinguish sorted configuration identity from UI value order.
Check persistence identities across remounts when optional IDs are omitted, and
compare legacy key encoding and ordering with the original producer. Exercise
throwing custom storage as well as the browser default; failure handling must
cover reads and every write path without changing facade identity on rerender.

For deferred dialog close callbacks, distinguish actual close from effect replay
and keyed replacement. Trace the library callback to both its captured session
and the currently live editor before it consumes return-focus ownership. Check
sibling hosts for the same lifetime contract; a guard in one host does not
establish it in another.

For async or composed fallback content, prove both the immediate state and the
transition from a previous result. Treat the rendered production composition,
not a supplied child slot or hook return alone, as the contract.

For context-dependent display projection, trace each live preference or locale
from its owner through the production projector and its invalidation boundary.
Require explicit invariant evidence for hard-coded defaults, and prove an
already-visible result refreshes when the context changes.

When rows are hidden after lazy metadata resolves, check that result counts and
empty states agree with visible eligibility. Preserve the loading path for
unresolved rows; test mixed results and fully resolved results with no eligible
rows, rather than checking row suppression alone.
# Hotkeys And Races

Review global and dialog hotkeys, virtualized registration, listener cleanup,
async transitions, and unmount behavior. Look for stale/delegated handlers,
workspace-versus-dialog conflicts, lifecycle leaks, and races between state
publication and event handling.

For changed async work, trace currentness to every final publisher, including
error and `finally` paths. Require delayed success and rejection cases that
retire the owner before publication and prove no stale status, dialog,
navigation, or cleanup effect appears.

For changed keyboard routing, build an outcome matrix for every live owner
state. Verify the final action and native-event result (`preventDefault` and
propagation), including ordinary editable input, composition, delegated
Confirm/Cancel/Escape, and capture-phase behavior.

When an overlay's visibility or eligibility changes, trace its interaction owner
through query, selection, and live-definition changes. Check whether a hidden or
retired overlay can still consume navigation, acceptance, or Escape, and whether
returning to the previous selection revives stale ownership. Compare the state
used by rendering with the state used by keyboard dispatch and execution; a
render predicate alone does not establish that ownership was retired. Inspect
reachable transitions through the mounted controller, not only isolated visible
and hidden props. Unrelated static presentation changes need no new matrix.
# Docs, Config, And Tooling

Use for docs, scripts, schemas, package files, generated resources, CI, or

# Domain Correctness

Review domain models, traversal, validation, transformation, serialization,
persistence, generated output, and stable user-facing identifiers. Use supplied
domain invariants and proof requirements. Trace changed data from accepted input
through the actual production path to final output and rejection/cleanup.

Challenge these failure classes when applicable:

- schema, persistence, runtime validation, and interactive admission disagree;
  include exact-limit and one-over-limit proof for collection constraints;
- creation defaults and explicit names violate the validator's uniqueness
  rules. Check occupied generated names and normalized requested collisions
  through each creation entry point, including legacy consumers;
- incomplete variants emit placeholders, discard valid falsy values, or perform
  lookups requiring a completed value;
- read-only traversal mutates persisted/plain data or assumes Immer drafts;
- typed accessors promise shapes they did not validate;
- destructive imports miss alternate references, aliases, overlays, or lexical
  trivia. Require source preservation or rejection when unsupported syntax
  leaves reference integrity or conditions uncertain;
- validators leak dependency wording, turn malformed data into ordinary guidance,
  or use presence checks where definedness is required;
- a generic resolver derives identity from feature-specific literals or
  locale-sensitive formatting;
- independently derived representations, indexes, lookups, traversal,
  collision/deduplication, merge, generation, or exemption paths disagree on
  canonical semantic identity;
- a staged change gains authority to update a persisted entity through name
  equality rather than its owned target. Trace target ownership across staging
  origins and nesting, refreshed persisted state, validation exemptions, and
  publication; compose conflicting and authorized paths in observable proof;
- a structured subject, path, or descriptor coordinate is projected into a
  different coordinate space without proving compatible identity and
  cardinality, such as treating an aggregate branch position as an item row.

For new persisted fields or changed cross-layer constraints, inventory owning
entities, mutating entry points, and affected invariants. Check preservation on
replacement and reference remapping or removal on move, copy, and delete.
Require an observable output/failure assertion that kills a plausible mutant,
not only a helper-level test.
# Architecture

Use the supplied architecture and coding standards. Focus on cohesion,
duplicated rules, public/type boundaries, folder topology, readable predicates,
and applicable local limits. File only changes that remove real indirection,
duplicated ownership, or ambiguity while retaining a clear domain boundary.

For every assigned `code-surface-conciseness` row, record each path as
`reduction candidate`, `no meaningful reduction`, or `out of scope` with a
reason. Do not equate fewer lines, arbitrary file splitting, or denser syntax
with a reduction.

For changed transactions/lifecycles with multiple identities, build a terminal
effect closure across success, rollback, partial completion, supersession, and
owner retirement. Trace each invalidated identity through cached, persisted,
notification, callback, and derived resources. Also challenge stale consumers
of retired result contracts, unsafe type recovery at schema boundaries, and
identity helpers that compare too few fields.
# Test Quality

Review changed unit, integration, browser, and helper proof. Look for tests
that can pass with missing behavior, optional assertions, fixed sleeps, leaked
global resources, brittle copy/class selectors, and claims stronger than their
assertions.

Check finding closure at the nearest stable public boundary. For absence,
fallback, or no-op tests, start with conflicting state so skipped work or a
leaked fallback makes the test fail.

For identity-sensitive async proof, compare the harness's callback and resource
lifetimes with their production producers. A stable mock cannot establish
coalescing across renders when the real dependency is recreated. Require an
unchanged-input request across a rerender alongside semantic-change replacement,
checking the operation count and final result. Use the real dependency or a
faithful lifetime model only at the boundary under test; do not remove unrelated
mocks or infer a user-visible path from direct hook calls alone.

For actions that remove the focused control or an overlay's return-focus target,
require a mounted keyboard test with an explicit final-focus assertion after
cleanup. Setting and visibility assertions alone do not prove focus continuity;
include disabled destinations and the surviving fallback.

For dialog focus closure, require the real dialog lifecycle, including deferred
cleanup and StrictMode replay when enabled by the host. An editor mock that
omits close-autofocus cannot prove ownership survives cleanup while still open.
When transitions share reveal, selection, or session state, check whether one
changes the other's guard or identity. If it does, require the reachable combined
scenario through final focus, or demonstrate independence from the consumer's
actual guards. Separate passing tests or a shared helper alone do not establish
independence; unrelated states need no combination matrix.

For gesture ownership changes, switch the owner while the gesture remains
active, then deliver completion and assert the successor's state is preserved.
Clearing the manual flag or ending the gesture before switching proves only
retirement, not completion through the successor's callbacks.

For shared persistence records, seed competing configurations with overlapping
IDs and different values. Assert both the restored active result and unchanged
siblings after mount and update; a single-configuration fixture cannot prove
selection or preservation.
Include omitted optional IDs across remounts, legacy keys with different sort
orders, and throwing custom reads/writes. Fixture guards must not supply the
failure isolation claimed for the production adapter.

For a production-path claim, apply supplied proof requirements:
the first observable checkpoint must precede fixture, mock, click, focus, or
recovery steps that could inject or repair the claimed state. Name a plausible
mutant and the assertion that kills it.

Check schema fixtures against their real types; test callbacks and admission
statuses through their competing fallback paths; use stable semantic selectors;
and prove geometry/scroll movement for responsive overflow. In pointer and drag
browser tests, sample destination geometry after activation or another
rendering transition before using it; do not carry pre-transition coordinates
into the changed layout. Require direct tests for changed pure recursive helpers
and explicit teardown for resources outside renderer ownership. For async
derived UI, prove initial and transition states, not only an eventual result.
# Adversarial Tooling And Boundaries

Use for scripts, git/shell/process wrappers, CLI or environment parsing,
path/glob handling, CI, audit output, and parsers of external command output.
Assign the Scope Inventory key `adversarial-tooling-boundary`.

Challenge argv/option injection, path containment, malformed or future command
output, trim/normalization drift, rename/delete/copy metadata, machine-output
rows with empty fields, delimiter collisions, and filtered values that differ
from values later reported or executed. An empty malformed path must never
become the repository root or current directory.

Include **Edge Assumptions Challenged** in the response: e.g. leading `-`,
embedded delimiters, missing/blank values, whitespace, unknown status codes,
renames, and malformed external rows. Check whether external tuple fields can
collide when combined into a cache or de-duplication key.
# React Rendering

Review TSX components, hooks, virtualized panels, layout state, rendering
lifecycle, performance-sensitive identity, accessibility, and translate-safe
content. Look for stale closures, controlled/uncontrolled drift, desynchronised
derived state, unnecessary hot-path renders, and component ownership ambiguity.

Challenge semantic keys that omit ordering, duplication, or normalisation
meaningful to the consumer. For global DOM state or registrations, trace update,
ownership transfer, deactivation, and unmount so stale cleanup cannot clear a
successor. For reusable components, verify prop surfaces describe actual local
behavior; caller classes merge correctly; and repeated mounted instances have
unique IDs.

For in-flight request identity, inspect both equality directions: equivalent
requests must still join after a rerender, and changed semantic inputs must
replace the running operation. Trace callback producers before treating their
references as request data; distinguish implementation churn from changes to
the captured execution environment. Inspect request equality separately from
owner lifetime and publication authority. This check applies when request
coalescing or replacement changes, not to every hook dependency array.

For overlay eligibility changes, apply the interaction-ownership check in
[Hotkeys And Races](hotkeys-and-races.md) across rendering and keyboard handling.

For dependency adapters, check retained optional props and upstream defaults
with both ordinary and app-specific implementations. For persistence, trace
restoration before startup writes and check owner identity at every writer.
A custom storage guard or final-flush guard does not protect other write paths.
When a storage record holds multiple configurations, check exact configuration
selection and sibling preservation at every writer, including restoration replay
and final flush. Distinguish sorted configuration identity from UI value order.
Check persistence identities across remounts when optional IDs are omitted, and
compare legacy key encoding and ordering with the original producer. Exercise
throwing custom storage as well as the browser default; failure handling must
cover reads and every write path without changing facade identity on rerender.

For deferred dialog close callbacks, distinguish actual close from effect replay
and keyed replacement. Trace the library callback to both its captured session
and the currently live editor before it consumes return-focus ownership. Check
sibling hosts for the same lifetime contract; a guard in one host does not
establish it in another.

For async or composed fallback content, prove both the immediate state and the
transition from a previous result. Treat the rendered production composition,
not a supplied child slot or hook return alone, as the contract.

For context-dependent display projection, trace each live preference or locale
from its owner through the production projector and its invalidation boundary.
Require explicit invariant evidence for hard-coded defaults, and prove an
already-visible result refreshes when the context changes.

When rows are hidden after lazy metadata resolves, check that result counts and
empty states agree with visible eligibility. Preserve the loading path for
unresolved rows; test mixed results and fully resolved results with no eligible
rows, rather than checking row suppression alone.
# Hotkeys And Races

Review global and dialog hotkeys, virtualized registration, listener cleanup,
async transitions, and unmount behavior. Look for stale/delegated handlers,
workspace-versus-dialog conflicts, lifecycle leaks, and races between state
publication and event handling.

retire the owner before publication and prove no stale status, dialog,
navigation, or cleanup effect appears.
